Convert an R object to JSON text

Source: R/json.R
toJSON.Rd

This function returns one R string, so it retains R's string-size limit. Use jsonlite::write_json() for large output.

Usage

toJSON(
  x,
  dataframe = c("rows", "columns", "values"),
  Date = c("ISO8601", "epoch"),
  POSIXt = c("string", "ISO8601", "epoch", "mongo"),
  factor = c("string", "integer"),
  null = c("list", "null"),
  na = c("null", "string"),
  auto_unbox = FALSE,
  digits = NA,
  pretty = FALSE,
  always_decimal = FALSE,
  UTC = FALSE,
  rownames = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An atomic vector, array, list, or data frame. Array dimensions are written in their existing order, including dimensions of length one or zero. Data frames may contain matrix, list, and data-frame columns.

dataframe

Data frame layout: rows, columns, or values.

Date

Encode Date objects as ISO 8601 strings such as "2026-01-31" ("ISO8601", the default) or as the number of days since 1970-01-01 ("epoch").

POSIXt

Encode date-times as strings in the format R prints them ("string", the default), as ISO 8601 strings ("ISO8601"), as milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC ("epoch"), or as MongoDB-style objects such as {"$date": 1767323045000} ("mongo").

factor

Encode factors as level labels ("string", the default) or integer level indices ("integer").

null

Encode NULL as an empty object, {} ("list", the default), or as JSON null ("null").

na

Encode missing and non-finite values as JSON null or as strings.

auto_unbox

Whether length-one atomic vectors become scalars. Use jsonlite::unbox() to mark individual values instead.

digits

NA (the default) writes every number as the shortest text that reads back to the same value. A number gives the maximum number of decimal digits, and a number wrapped in I() the number of significant digits; both round as jsonlite does.

pretty

Whether to indent the output: TRUE for two spaces per level, or the number of spaces. Pretty file output ends with a newline.

always_decimal

Distinguish doubles from integers by retaining a decimal point or exponent in finite double output.

UTC

Whether date-times are converted to UTC. With POSIXt = "ISO8601" the strings then end in Z.

rownames

Whether row names of data frames are written, as a _row field. The default, NULL, writes character row names but not automatic ones.

Value

A length-one character vector of class c("glazelite_json", "json"). It prints as plain JSON text; use as.character() to drop the class.

Details

The arguments and the structure of the output follow jsonlite::toJSON(). Two defaults differ: numbers keep full precision unless digits is set, and missing numbers are written as null unless na = "string".

See also

jsonlite::fromJSON() for the reverse conversion, jsonlite::write_json() to write to a file.

Examples

toJSON(c(1.5, NA, 3))
#> [1.5,null,3]
toJSON(list(id = 1L, tags = c("a", "b")), auto_unbox = TRUE)
#> {"id":1,"tags":["a","b"]}
toJSON(matrix(1:6, nrow = 2))
#> [[1,3,5],[2,4,6]]
toJSON(pi, digits = 3)
#> [3.142]

df <- data.frame(id = 1:2, group = factor(c("a", "b")),
                 day = as.Date(c("2026-01-31", NA)))
toJSON(df)
#> [{"id":1,"group":"a","day":"2026-01-31"},{"id":2,"group":"b"}]
toJSON(df, dataframe = "columns", factor = "integer", Date = "epoch")
#> {"id":[1,2],"group":[1,2],"day":[20484,null]}
toJSON(df, pretty = TRUE)
#> [
#>   {
#>     "id": 1,
#>     "group": "a",
#>     "day": "2026-01-31"
#>   },
#>   {
#>     "id": 2,
#>     "group": "b"
#>   }
#> ]
